human_tolerance.notes: Adaptable and increasingly common in wooded suburbs and even city parks, where it will excavate in large dead trees and stumps.

phases.name: territorial
phases.note: Resident all year, territorial and noisy in every season, drumming and giving calls from a large standing dead tree.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Pairs excavate a large unlined cavity, usually high in a dead tree; both parents incubate for 12 to 16 days.

vocalizations.description: A flat, ringing 'woick woick' given repeatedly, one of several courtship displays used with drumming and bill-waving to attract a mate or talk to a partner.
A sharp, short call given in alarm, often repeated in a series while the bird is agitated.

conservation.note: Wikidata carries no P141 value for this item; Wikipedia states that the species' large range and increasing population have it categorised as least concern by the IUCN.

range.note: Resident across Canada and the United States, with an extensive range and rising numbers; it also inhabits smaller woodlots provided they contain some tall trees.

traits.limb_count.note: Biped: two legs; the wings are not counted as limbs.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Clings to and climbs trunks and flies strongly between trees.

traits.nest_type.note: Excavates large nests in the cavities of dead trees, high off the ground; the cavity is unlined except for wood chips.

traits.mass_kg.note: EltonTraits BodyMass-Value 286.59 g converted to kilograms; Wikipedia gives an average of about 277 g across both sexes, so the two agree closely.

traits.length_m.note: Adults are 40-49 cm long; the midpoint is used.

traits.wingspan_m.note: Midpoint of the 66-75 cm wingspan given on Wikipedia.

traits.lifespan_y.note: No allow-listed open source states wild longevity for this species. Authored estimate only: 6 years, taken as the mid-range figure for a large woodpecker and not a sourced datum. Treat it as an order-of-magnitude value.

traits.diet.note: EltonTraits Diet-Inv 70 mapped to 'invertebrate', Diet-Fruit 20 to 'fruit', Diet-Seed 10 to 'seed'; the dataset classes this species as an invertebrate feeder.

traits.social.note: A territorial pair holds a nest cavity and shares incubation; both parents incubate for 12 to 16 days.

traits.activity_pattern.note: EltonTraits Nocturnal 0; Wikipedia describes diurnal drumming and calling.

traits.defense.note: Flies off and takes cover in dense timber when disturbed; judgement mapping to the schema's single-value field.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: adaptable and increasingly tolerant of people, but a large, conspicuous bird that flushes readily from a close approach in open woodland.

habitat.use.note: EltonTraits ForStrat-Value gives ground 20 / understory 30 / midhigh 30 / canopy 20; the understory, midhigh and canopy strata are summed into the arboreal share.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Roosts and nests in cavities in dead trees.

habitat.resources.note: Food weights follow traits.diet; the nesting weights are judgement, since no open source gives their relative use.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Wikipedia calls the species quite adaptable, occupying an extensive range; dead trees and stumps in wooded suburbs provide its nesting and foraging sites.

seasonal.strategy.note: A permanent resident of its range, with no migration.

seasonal.phases.note: The courtship displays, the unlined cavity nest high in a dead tree and the 12-16 day incubation are from Wikipedia; the calendar windows are authored judgement, since no open source gives egg dates.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Incubation lasts 12 to 16 days; the 70-day juvenile window to fledging and the 0.85 scale are authored judgement, since Wikipedia gives no nestling period.

vocalizations.woick.note: Wikipedia names the 'woick' call as one of this species' courtship displays, alongside drumming and bill waving. No open source gives frequency bands, so freq_hz is omitted.

vocalizations.alarm_call.note: Wikipedia establishes that the species is noisy with varied calls but does not describe this one; the wording and cooldown are authored.

look.note: Colours from Wikipedia's description of a mostly black bird with a bold red crest, white facial stripes and a very long chisel bill. The proportions and the crest and cheek boxes are authored judgement.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared perching-songbird program. Woodpeckers neither sing nor forage on the ground, so this is a compromise: it is a perching-and-fleeing tree, and the slot the program uses for a song is given to the courtship 'woick' call and drumming.
